rows.claim: At B's tick times `y_state`/`y_direct` read whatever their inputs are at that instant
rows.evidence: src/declare.jl:865-867 gives the bundle field `u` to `y_direct` and the update stage only; src/declare.jl:630 (y_state docstring) says its bundle carries no inputs; src/build.jl:1043-1047 probes y_state with empty `u`
rows.note: y_state carries no inputs on either tier; only y_direct reads `u`. Spec §5.2 table, spec.md:1315 and 1319, says the same, so the companion misstates it.
rows.fix: Replace with: `y_direct` reads whatever its inputs *are at that instant*, `y_state` reads the state alone, and both compute B's outputs, write them to B's cells, ...

rows.claim: A feedback loop closed through B is schedulable precisely because B's output is held state rather than feedthrough (§5.3)
rows.evidence: probe:78 (A with feedthrough y_direct <-> discrete B with y_direct: `AlgebraicCycle`, members a=:global, b=:structural); probe:374 (same loop with B's output in `y_state`: builds); src/build.jl:187-192 (edges follow every consumed stage-2 port, tier-blind)
rows.note: The freeze does not make a loop through B schedulable. A discrete component's `y_direct` port is a stage-2 feedthrough edge like any other, so a loop closed through the `y_direct` B of this very chain is rejected at build. Only a loop closed through a stage-1 (`y_state`) port is legal, on either tier. Spec §5.3 (spec.md:1290 ff.) ties legality to the stage split, not to the tier.
rows.fix: There is a structural echo of the same fact. A feedback loop is schedulable precisely because the port it closes through is stage 1, held state with no input dependence ([§5.3]), and not a `y_direct` feedthrough; a discrete B's `y_direct` is feedthrough too, so a loop closed through it is the algebraic loop [§5.5] rejects. The freeze and the schedule are two statements of the same fact: partials flow only along instantaneous dependence.

rows.evidence: probe:385 (SeaMotion output declared `Pinned{DeckField{Float64}}`, stage builds at `x.heave`: `ConformanceFailure` at the Dual probe, hint 'remove its Pinned'); probe:395 (zero coupling only after the author strips with ForwardDiff.value: C = [0.0 -0.1])

The coupling goes silently to zero only if the author also strips the pose with `ForwardDiff.value`, as spec §9.5 'Deliberate stripping' (spec.md:5925-5945) describes.
rows.fix: Pinning here would be refused at the first `Dual` probe, since the pose carries partials; an author who stripped the pose to satisfy the pin would silently zero the coupling between ship motion and touchdown.

rows.claim: D-263's rule that a mutable type's parameters pin keeps the Matrix{Dual} grid copy off the table
rows.evidence: probe:363 (`DeckT{Float64}` with `grid::Matrix{T}` retypes to `DeckT{Dual}` with a `Matrix{Dual}` field); probe:364 (`retype` pins `Matrix{Float64}` only where a mutable type is itself the entry); src/leaves.jl:232-236 (retype leaves a mutable type's parameters alone, and never enters fields)
rows.note: For the sketch's immutable `DeckField{T}` the mutable-parameter rule does not apply: the walk substitutes the struct's parameter and the field `Matrix{T}` follows. What keeps the copy off the table is the author typing `grid::Matrix{Float64}` concretely. Spec.md:3243-3245 words it the same way, so spec and companion both want the fix.
rows.fix: The concrete `grid::Matrix{Float64}` keeps that copy off the table, because the walk substitutes type parameters and never fields ([D-263]'s mutable-parameter rule pins a mutable type on the walk itself), and the one-scalar-plus-reference shape gets the same derivatives for free.

rows.claim: A stage that hands a `Dual` for `b` dies in `convert(Float64, ::Dual)`, which has no method
rows.evidence: probe:317 (`MixedRight(px, px)`: `MethodError` on the constructor itself, since the default outer constructor is `MixedRight(::T, ::Float64)`); probe:319 (`MixedRight{P}(px, px)`: `MethodError(Float64, Dual)` through convert); probe:333 (build reports `UserCodeFraming` with 'no method matching MixedRight(::Dual, ::Dual)')
rows.note: It is a `MethodError` either way, but the natural spelling `MixedRight(x.q, x.q)` dies at the outer constructor, not in `convert`. Only the explicit `MixedRight{T}(a, b)` form reaches `convert`. Log D-265 (log.md:11525-11527) has the same wording.
rows.fix: The struct's own constructor enforces the freeze on the producer side: a stage that hands a `Dual` for `b` dies in a `MethodError`, at the constructor `MixedRight(::Dual, ::Dual)`, or in `convert(Float64, ::Dual)` under the explicit `MixedRight{T}(a, b)`, and `Float64` has no method for a `Dual`.
